newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambian mine closed, scores left homeless by floods.
newsitem.headline: Zambian mine closed, scores left homeless by floods.

text.p: Zambia's largest coal mine has been closed and scores of people left homeless in the southern town of Maamba after heavy flooding in the area, the government's information service said on Wednesday.
The Zambia Information Service said in a statement the Maamba coal mine had been completely flooded and vital equipment damaged.
Scores of people were forced to leave their homes and maize crops in the area had been washed away by several days of heavy rain.

"Most of the equipment, including the control centre at the mine, has been extensively damaged by the floods. The pit is completely flooded and pumps are urgently required to deal with the situation," it said.
It said the mine clinic was also flooded forcing medical staff to evacuate patients to a makeshift clinic. Water and sewage systems in the mine area had also been damaged.
"There are fears that Maamba might be cut off from the rest of the country as the two highway bridges within the mine area are partially damaged," it added.
The floods had also washed away food supplies and crops, leaving people in danger of starvation, the statement said.
